question: Why do elephants have trunks?
text: Elephants use trunks to smell and drink. A trunk can pick things up.

question: Can penguins fly?
text: Penguins cannot fly in the air. Their wings help them swim.

question: How do dolphins breathe?
text: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole. They come up for each breath.

question: Are whales fish?
text: Whales are not fish. They breathe air and feed milk.

question: Why do turtles have shells?
text: A shell helps keep a turtle safe. It is part of its body.

question: How do snails move?
text: A snail glides on one wide foot. Slime helps it slide along.

question: Why do zebras have stripes?
text: Each zebra has its own stripe pattern. Stripes may help keep flies away.

question: What do giraffes eat?
text: Giraffes eat leaves from tall trees. Their long necks help them reach.

question: How do frogs grow?
text: Frogs start as eggs in water. Young frogs grow legs as they change.

question: How many legs do spiders have?
text: Spiders have eight legs. Insects have six legs.

question: Where do ants live?
text: Many ants live in nests underground. They work in groups called colonies.

question: Why do owls hunt at night?
text: Many owls hunt when it is dark. Sharp ears help them find food.

question: Are bats birds?
text: Bats are not birds. They have fur and feed milk.

question: Why do kangaroos have pouches?
text: A pouch holds a young kangaroo. It keeps the young one close.

question: What is in a camel hump?
text: A camel stores fat in its hump. It does not store water there.

question: Why do ducks have webbed feet?
text: Wide feet push against the water. This helps ducks swim.

question: Do sharks have bones?
text: Sharks have soft frames called cartilage. Our ears have this bendy stuff too.

question: Where do polar bears live?
text: Polar bears live near the North Pole. They use sea ice to find food.

question: Where do eggs come from?
text: Hens lay eggs. Some eggs can hatch into chicks.

question: What do rabbits eat?
text: Rabbits eat plants, such as grass. Their teeth keep growing.

question: What is a planet?
text: A planet moves around a star. Earth is the planet where we live.

question: What is the sun?
text: The sun is a star near Earth. It gives us light and warmth.

question: Why is Mars red?
text: Dust on Mars has rusty iron. That rust gives it a red color.

question: Why does Saturn have rings?
text: Rings around Saturn hold ice and rock. These bits move around the planet.

question: What shape is Earth?
text: Earth is round like a ball. It is a bit wider at the middle.

question: What does an astronaut do?
text: An astronaut travels to space. They can study Earth from far above.

question: How do rockets move?
text: A rocket pushes hot gas behind it. That push moves the rocket forward.

question: What is the solar system?
text: The sun and its planets form a group. We call it the solar system.

question: What is an eclipse?
text: One space body blocks light from another. A shadow can then fall on Earth.

question: What is a shooting star?
text: It is a small rock from space. It glows as it moves through air.

question: What is a constellation?
text: Stars can seem to make a shape. People give these star groups names.

question: What is a satellite?
text: A satellite goes around a space body. Our moon goes around Earth.

question: What does the heart do?
text: Your heart pumps blood through your body. Blood brings what your cells need.

question: What do lungs do?
text: Lungs help you breathe in air. They pass oxygen into your blood.

question: What does the brain do?
text: Your brain helps you think and learn. It sends signals through your body.

question: Why do we have bones?
text: Bones hold your body up. They help keep soft parts safe.

question: What do teeth do?
text: Teeth help cut and crush food. This makes it easier to eat.

question: How do ears hear?
text: Sound makes tiny parts in your ears move. Your brain turns signals into sounds.

question: How do eyes see?
text: Eyes take in light. Your brain uses signals to make pictures.

question: What does skin do?
text: Skin covers and protects your body. It helps you feel touch and warmth.

question: Why should I wash my hands?
text: Soap and water wash germs away. Clean hands help keep germs from spreading.

question: Why do we breathe?
text: Your body needs oxygen from the air. Breathing also lets waste gas leave.

question: How do muscles work?
text: Muscles pull to move your body. They get shorter as they pull.

question: How do we taste food?
text: Tiny buds on your tongue sense tastes. Your nose helps with flavor too.

question: Why do we sneeze?
text: A sneeze helps clear your nose. Air rushes out in a quick burst.

question: How does snow form?
text: Water can freeze in cold clouds. Small ice bits join to make snowflakes.

question: What makes wind?
text: Wind is air moving from place to place. Uneven warmth helps make air move.

question: What makes thunder?
text: Lightning heats the air very fast. The air expands and makes a loud sound.

question: What is fog?
text: Fog is a cloud near the ground. It holds tiny drops of water.

question: What is hail?
text: Hail is made of balls of ice. They grow in strong storm clouds.

question: Why do seasons change?
text: Earth leans as it moves around the sun. This changes how much sunlight we get.

question: What is dew?
text: Cool air can leave drops on surfaces. We call these small drops dew.

question: Why do puddles dry up?
text: Water slowly turns into gas in the air. Warmth can make this happen faster.

question: Why does a raincoat keep us dry?
text: A raincoat has a layer that blocks water. Drops roll off its surface.

question: What is a desert?
text: A desert gets very little rain. Some deserts are hot and some are cold.

question: How do cacti save water?
text: Cacti store water in thick stems. A waxy skin helps keep it inside.

question: Why do plants have flowers?
text: Pollen helps plants make seeds. Bees move it from bloom to bloom.

question: What do roots do?
text: Roots hold a plant in place. They take in water from the soil.

question: What are tree rings?
text: Many trees grow a new ring each year. Rings can show how a tree grew.

question: Why do plants make fruit?
text: Fruit holds seeds. Animals can carry the seeds to new places.

question: What is soil?
text: Soil holds bits of rock and old plants. Many small living things live there.

question: Is a mushroom a plant?
text: A mushroom is not a plant. It belongs to a group called fungi.

question: Why are sunflowers called sunflowers?
text: Their large flowers look like the sun. Young plants can turn toward sunlight.

question: What is pollen?
text: Pollen is a fine dust from flowers. It helps many plants make seeds.

question: Do ferns have flowers?
text: Ferns do not have flowers. They spread with tiny bits called spores.

question: What type is Pikachu?
text: That buddy is from a made-up world. It is an Electric type.

question: What type is Charmander?
text: That buddy is from a made-up world. It is a Fire type.

question: What type is Squirtle?
text: That buddy is from a made-up world. It is a Water type.

question: What type is Bulbasaur?
text: That buddy is from a made-up world. It has a Grass type.

question: What is Eevee?
text: Eevee is from a made-up world. It can change into many forms.

question: Are Pokemon real?
text: Those buddies are from a made-up world. Real animals live in our world.

question: What is a Poke Ball?
text: It is a ball in a made-up world. Stories use it to hold a buddy.

question: What is two plus three?
text: Two plus three make five. We can count five fingers on one hand.
